questions.stem_latex:
The population of a town can be estimated by using the formula $P=P_0e^{kt}$, where $t$ is the time in years after the year 2020 and $P_0$ and $k$ are constants.

The population at the beginning of the year 2020 was 300, and at the beginning of 2024 it was 450.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.latex: In what year will the town's population be double that of the year 2020?

The water height in an estuary fluctuates according to the tide. Flooding will occur when the water height reaches 1.5 m. One day the high tide of 1.6 m occurred at 3:00 am and the following low tide at 9:30 am. Assume that the following high tide was also 1.6 m and the height of the tide is modelled by the equation

$$h=1+0.6\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{13}(t+0.25)\right),$$

where $h$ is the height in metres and $t$ is the time in hours after midnight.

Find the time when the next flooding would be expected to occur, to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex:
$f'(x)=\displaystyle\int6x-2\,dx=3x^{2}-2x+c$. Stationary point at $(1,2)$ gives $f'(1)=0$: $0=3-2+c$, so $c=-1$ and $f'(x)=3x^{2}-2x-1$.

$f(x)=\displaystyle\int3x^{2}-2x-1\,dx=x^{3}-x^{2}-x+c$. Since $f(1)=2$: $2=1-1-1+c$, so $c=3$.

$f(x)=x^{3}-x^{2}-x+3$

solutions.latex:
Inflection requires $f''(x)=0$: $0=6x-2$, so $x=\dfrac13$. $f\left(\dfrac13\right)=\dfrac1{27}-\dfrac19-\dfrac13+3=\dfrac{70}{27}$.

Test concavity: $f''(0)=-2$, $f''\left(\dfrac13\right)=0$, $f''(1)=4$. The change in sign of $f''(x)$ shows $\left(\dfrac13,\dfrac{70}{27}\right)$ is a point of inflection.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2 marks total (point found, change in concavity shown)

solutions.latex:
Stationary points: $y'=0$, so $\cos x\,e^{\sin x}=0$. Since $e^{\sin x}>0$ there is no solution to $e^{\sin x}=0$, so $\cos x=0$, giving $x=\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}2$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$.

At $x=\dfrac\pi2$: $y=e^{\sin(\pi/2)}=e$. At $x=\dfrac{3\pi}2$: $y=e^{-1}=\dfrac1e$.

Stationary points: $\left(\dfrac\pi2,e\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}2,\dfrac1e\right)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2 marks total (show only 2 solutions with $e^{\sin x}\ne0$ stated, coordinates in simplest exact form)

solutions.latex:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&0&\dfrac\pi2&\pi\\\hline y'&1&0&-1\end{array}$ The change in sign of $y'$ shows $\left(\dfrac\pi2,e\right)$ is a local maximum.

$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&\pi&\dfrac{3\pi}2&2\pi\\\hline y'&-1&0&1\end{array}$ The change in sign of $y'$ shows $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}2,\dfrac1e\right)$ is a local minimum.

Alternatively use $y''$: negative at $x=\dfrac\pi2$ and positive at $x=\dfrac{3\pi}2$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2 marks total (one for each nature with numerical justification)

solutions.latex:
$y$ is positive definite if $\Delta<0$ and $a>0$.

$\Delta=b^{2}-4ac=(2+k)^{2}-12(k+1)<0$

$k^{2}+4k-12k-12<0\Rightarrow k^{2}-8k-12<0$

Solving $k^{2}-8k-8=0$: $k=\dfrac{8\pm\sqrt{64+32}}2=4\pm2\sqrt6$, so $4-2\sqrt6<k<4+2\sqrt6$.

Also $a>0$ means $k>-1$, which is already satisfied by this solution.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: discriminant expression; 1: simplified inequality; 1: correct solution

solutions.latex:
Let $u=8\sin x$, $v=\ln x$; $u'=8\cos x$, $v'=\dfrac1x$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=uv'+vu'=\dfrac{8\sin x}{x}+8\cos x\ln x$

At rest $v=0$: $0=t(3-t)$, so $t=3$.

$x=\displaystyle\int3t-t^{2}dt=\dfrac{3t^{2}}2-\dfrac{t^{3}}3+C$; $x(0)=0$ gives $C=0$. $x(3)=4.5$.

The body travelled 4.5 m.

$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=3-2t$; at $t=3$, $a=-3<0$.

Interpretation: the body has slowed down, coming to rest. It then changes direction and speeds up.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: $a=3-2t$ and $a=-3$; 1: interpretation (must mention change of direction)

Let $u=\sin x$, $v=1+\cos x$; $u'=\cos x$, $v'=-\sin x$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{u'v-v'u}{v^{2}}=\dfrac{\cos x(1+\cos x)+\sin^{2}x}{(1+\cos x)^{2}}=\dfrac{\cos x+\cos^{2}x+\sin^{2}x}{(1+\cos x)^{2}}=\dfrac{1+\cos x}{(1+\cos x)^{2}}=\dfrac1{1+\cos x}$

solutions.latex:
Double the 2020 population is 600: $600=300e^{\frac{\ln3-\ln2}4t}$, so $2=e^{\frac{\ln3-\ln2}4t}$, $\ln2=\dfrac{\ln3-\ln2}4t$, $t=\dfrac{4\ln2}{\ln3-\ln2}\approx6.84$ years.

Hence towards the end of the year 2026 the town will have double the 2020 population.

solutions.latex:
Solve $1.5=1+0.6\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{13}(t+0.25)\right)$: $\dfrac56=\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{13}+\dfrac\pi{26}\right)$.

The first solution is $t\approx1.7882$ (1:47 am), which is before the 9:30 am low tide. The period is 13 hours, so adding 13 hours (the next time the tide is rising through 1.5 m): $t\approx14.7882$.

The next flooding is expected at 14:47, i.e. 2:47 pm.

Alternative: general solution $t=\dfrac{13}{2\pi}(-1)^{k}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac56\right)+\dfrac{13k}2-\dfrac14$; $k=0$ gives $t\approx1.7882$ and $k=2$ gives $t\approx14.7882$.

solutions.marks_breakdown: 3 marks total (development of formulae up to $A_3$, GP sum, simplification)

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1292_q35_s1}

Intersection of curves: $x^{2}=9+3x-x^{2}\Rightarrow2x^{2}-3x-9=0\Rightarrow(2x+3)(x-3)=0$, so $x=-1.5,3$. When $y=1$, $x^{2}=1$, so $x=\pm1$.

First find the area between the curves: $\displaystyle\int_{-1.5}^{3}9+3x-x^{2}-x^{2}\,dx$, then subtract the area between the line $y=1$ and $y=x^{2}$: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}1-x^{2}\,dx$.

Area $=\left[9x+\dfrac32x^{2}-\dfrac23x^{3}\right]_{-1.5}^{3}-\dfrac43=29\dfrac1{24}\ \text{u}^{2}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4 marks total (points of intersection, set up integrals, integrate, correct area)

solutions.latex:
Perimeter of semi-circle $=r+\dfrac{\pi r}2$ and perimeter of sector $ACB=r+r\theta$.

$\therefore P=\dfrac{\pi r}2+r+r\theta=r\left(\dfrac\pi2+1+\theta\right)$

$P=2r^{-1}+r\left(\dfrac\pi4+1\right)$, $\dfrac{dP}{dr}=-\dfrac2{r^{2}}+\dfrac\pi4+1$, $\dfrac{d^{2}P}{dr^{2}}=4r^{-3}$.

Least perimeter when $\dfrac{dP}{dr}=0$: $\dfrac2{r^{2}}=\dfrac{\pi+4}4$, so $r^{2}=\dfrac8{\pi+4}$. For $r>0$, $\dfrac{d^{2}P}{dr^{2}}=4r^{-3}>0$, so $P$ is a minimum.

From (b), $\theta=\dfrac2{r^{2}}-\dfrac\pi4$ and $\dfrac2{r^{2}}=\dfrac\pi4+1$, so $\theta=1$ radian $\approx57^\circ$.

notes: Sydney Boys High School 2020 Term 3 Trial HSC (the bundled solutions cover calls it Assessment Task 3; labelled AT4 per the trial rule). Bundled marking guidelines on pages 29-56: MCQ key, handwritten worked MCQ solutions, annotated scan for Q11-15, typed solutions for Q16-36. The PDF text layer contains many repeated 'Question 15 (continued)' / 'MR. DRAKE'S PRACTICE PAPER' fragments that are hidden template artefacts, ignored. Printed page 7 (blank) is absent from the file. Section II part headings: Part A 14, B 17, C 16, D 15, E 12, F 16 = 90, but Part E questions 30-33 print marks 2+4+5+3 = 14 (heading says 12), so Section II question marks sum to 92; question marks kept as printed. Q32 part marks printed 2 and 3, but the guidelines give 1 and 2 (total 3 rather than 5); printed marks kept. Q31(a) has blank space for a sketch, no printed figure. Q28(b) quote marks printed as 'yes'. Q16 flagged old syllabus (types of relations); Q34 flagged Standard course borderline (loans/annuities). Q33 guideline note says 1:47 am assumed first solution; worked answer 2:47 pm. Q35 solution has two further step diagrams (shaded regions) not cropped. Q10 guideline notes there is no maximum distance from the origin (as t grows x tends to minus infinity), not an issue with the MCQ.
